data.long_meaning: Jankee is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Janki', which refers to the goddess of wisdom, Saraswati. The name symbolizes intelligence, knowledge, and enlightenment. The name Jankee carries the meaning “Goddess of Wisdom” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Jankee usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of wisdom and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Jankee belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess of Wisdom.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Jankee total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

data.cultural_impact: The name Jankee embraces tradition and India's rich mythological heritage. Hindu culture places significant importance on education and wisdom, associating these values with the goddess Saraswati. By giving a name inspired by Saraswati, it is believed the child may be blessed with the inherent abilities to learn, develop intellectually, and excel in various fields.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Jankee holds deep spiritual significance for Hindu families, as it connects the child to the goddess of knowledge and wisdom, Saraswati. The belief is that the blessing of the deity, through the name, empowers the child to gain knowledge and understanding of both the material and spiritual worlds. Further, it serves as a constant reminder for the child to uphold the virtues of intellect, enlightenment, and wisdom throughout their life.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Jankee: Goddess Saraswati's graceful and knowledgeable child. symbolizing wisdom, art, and creativity.

historical_references.reference: The name Janaki is mentioned in the ancient Indian epic Ramayana, referring to Sita Devi, the wife of Lord Rama.
The name Janaki is also found in the Puranas, a collection of ancient Indian texts, referring to the goddess Lakshmi, the goddess of wealth and prosperity.
